topic: Study exactly bivariate stationary Gaussian OU systems dX_t=-A X_t dt+D^{1/2}dW_t with known bidirected support, trace(D)=1, D diagonal and strictly positive, kappa I <= Sigma <= kappa^{-1} I, |A_12| and |A_21| at least eta, ||A||_F <= M, and iid stationary snapshots. Prove an exact characterization of the compatible sign set of A_12 A_21 using the affine Lyapunov fiber and four finite sector certificates, including explicit witnesses and every open-versus-closed attainment branch. Derive the equal-variance thresholds, exhibit an open region where neither edge sign is identified but their product sign is, and analyze the explicit asymmetric zero-diffusion contact. Invert a covariance confidence region with a measurable nearest-model fallback to obtain honest finite-sample set coverage, uniform singleton recovery beyond root-n clearance, and a matching local Gaussian lower bound on compact contact subcharts. Exclude larger-graph projection, marginalization, global boundary-distance equivalence, and empirical-performance claims. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The affine Lyapunov parametrization yields explicit scalar sector-feasibility rules: u A_12+s A_21=t[s+(u-s)d]/(2 Delta), exact same-sign strict-feasibility branches, always strictly feasible opposite-sign polygons, and a closed-form equal-variance norm after x=d-1/2 and y=q+rx/2. These reductions give positive and negative thresholds, including unattained norm equality. At the asymmetric contact, g >= (s-u)td is necessary and d=g/[2(s-u)t], q=(eta Delta-dt/2)/s constructs positive witnesses for g>0. Symbolic algebra and 400 randomized active-set comparisons supported these unverified derivations. Checks covered empty K, kappa=1, t=0, s=u, margin equality, norm equality, zero-diffusion contact, fixed-alpha empty covariance regions, and local-versus-global boundary distance; no verified current-literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove completeness of the finite equality-active-set certificate and its scalar J and strict-attainment branches on every rank-deficient, lower-dimensional, and norm-equality sector. EARLY KILL TEST: Exactly certify the asymmetric g=0 J-false contact, an attained equal-variance positive threshold, and the r=1/2, eta=3/5, M^2=67/45 unattained negative infimum; any failure stops this theorem spine. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_ou_cycle_polarity_contact_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly which values of sign(A_12 A_21) are compatible with a given stationary covariance in the bivariate directed 2-cycle Gaussian OU model when positive diagonal diffusion is unknown but trace-normalized and covariance, edge magnitudes, and drift norm are bounded.

source_refs.claim: After developing pointwise signs for individual drift edges, the paper explicitly lists subgraph and graph-level sign identifiability as future directions.
source_refs.author: Gijs van Seeventer and Saber Salehkaleybar
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 337

source_refs.claim: With fixed volatility, global drift identifiability holds exactly for simple graphs, so a directed 2-cycle is the sharp obstruction and produces a nontrivial Lyapunov fiber.
source_refs.author: Philipp Dettling, Roser Homs, Carlos Amendola, Mathias Drton, and Niels Richard Hansen
source_refs.venue: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 44(4)

open_problems.why_unsolved: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar's signature sets concern one drift edge at a time and do not treat the joint graph-level functional sign(A_12 A_21); they also do not impose trace normalization, lower edge magnitudes, and a Frobenius cap simultaneously. Dettling et al. fix the volatility matrix and characterize failure of full parameter recovery on 2-cycles, but not which coarser sign functionals remain constant along the fiber. The first missing step is therefore to replace one-edge zero feasibility by simultaneous same-sign and opposite-sign feasibility on the affine Lyapunov fiber while retaining strict diffusion positivity and every compact constraint. The supplied scalar reductions and randomized checks are presolve evidence only: completeness of the finite equality-active-set certificate remains unproved on degenerate sectors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic certificate for the compatible polarity set S(Sigma) subseteq {+,-}, with explicit drift-diffusion witnesses and a completeness proof covering every full-dimensional and equality-active sector.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest motivation arc from stationary snapshots and scale ambiguity to recoverable qualitative causal information, then explicitly points toward graph-level signs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Stationary snapshots erase temporal scale -> exact drift coefficients cease to be identified when diffusion is unknown -> individual edge signs can survive -> ask whether feedback-cycle polarity is identified even when the two edge signs are not

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the edge-signature-set definition and its reduction of fixed-covariance Lyapunov compatibility to linear feasibility, replacing the single-edge sign constraint by four joint sign sectors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its feasible-set object is the direct one-edge analogue of the required compatible cycle-polarity set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use half-vectorization of the continuous Lyapunov equation to expose its affine parameter fiber, then analyze the null direction induced by the directed 2-cycle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired sign set is a quotient of precisely the non-singleton 2-cycle Lyapunov fiber isolated by their identifiability theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a sample criterion or regular-parameter confidence region to cover a set-valued target, and prove consistency and rates for the resulting random set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once polarity compatibility is expressed by finite feasibility restrictions, its sampling version is a finite-dimensional set-inversion problem.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the complete open-versus-closed attainment frontier for positive and negative cycle-polarity sectors in the constrained bivariate Gaussian OU Lyapunov fiber, including equal-variance covariances, norm-equality thresholds, and contact with a zero diffusion coordinate.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves that partial edge-sign identifiability is a positive-measure phenomenon but provides covariance-level conditions only for selected edge targets and leaves graph-level signs open.
source_refs.author: Gijs van Seeventer and Saber Salehkaleybar
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 337

source_refs.claim: The continuous Lyapunov trek rule gives explicit covariance formulas only in special cases; its finite polynomial form is restricted to acyclic models.
source_refs.author: Niels Richard Hansen

source_refs.claim: The nonsimple-graph analysis focuses on global or generic parameter identifiability rather than strict-inequality attainment along bounded 2-cycle fibers.
source_refs.author: Philipp Dettling, Roser Homs, Carlos Amendola, Mathias Drton, and Niels Richard Hansen
source_refs.venue: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 44(4)

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing Lyapunov identifiability work is algebraic or generic, so it does not distinguish an attained boundary point from an infimum excluded by strict positivity of both diffusion coordinates or by the nonzero-edge constraint. The edge-sign paper likewise does not supply the topology of a bounded bivariate joint-sign sector. The first new step is a complete equality-active-set analysis of an affine line intersected with strict halfspaces, edge-magnitude sectors, and a quadratic norm ball. Rank-deficient equal-variance faces, unattained norm equality, and the asymmetric zero-diffusion contact cannot be justified merely by continuity from full-dimensional cases.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A disjoint semialgebraic stratification of covariance and tuning-parameter space with closed-form positive and negative thresholds, explicit equality witnesses, and an exact label of attained, closure-only, or infeasible for every boundary branch.

writing_exemplar.why: Its identifiable/partially-identifiable/non-identifiable trichotomy is the natural framing to sharpen into a complete boundary-sensitive classification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Qualitative edge information can survive coefficient nonidentification -> partial identifiability occupies a non-negligible covariance region -> graph-level polarity requires joint feasibility -> exact conclusions depend on whether strict sectors attain their algebraic thresholds

method_exemplars.technique: Parametrize the null direction of the vectorized Lyapunov coefficient matrix before imposing graph support and positivity constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This reduces the inverse problem to the one-dimensional fiber whose equality-active intersections must be classified.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit Lyapunov covariance expansions and variance inequalities to cross-check symmetric and sign-restricted boundary faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof shows how sign restrictions yield exact covariance inequalities, while the cyclic fiber demands a finite direct replacement for its infinite expansion.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt deterministic sample-covariance perturbation control for Lyapunov loss, replacing sparse-support recovery by stability of finite sector inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest stationary-Gaussian snapshot analysis connecting empirical covariance error to recovery of a causal drift feature.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an honest finite-sample confidence set for the compatible bivariate OU cycle-polarity set by inverting a Gaussian covariance confidence region, with a measurable nearest-model fallback when the empirical region misses the constrained model and uniform singleton recovery under root-n clearance.

source_refs.claim: The paper defines population edge-signature sets and pointwise identifiability from Sigma but contains no sampling-theory or confidence-set construction.
source_refs.author: Gijs van Seeventer and Saber Salehkaleybar
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 337

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs confidence regions for identified sets by inverting sample criteria and derives consistency, convergence rates, and inference results.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: For nondifferentiable transformations of asymptotically Gaussian parameters, the standard bootstrap can fail; the paper develops locally valid alternatives.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

open_problems.why_unsolved: Population polarity compatibility is a discontinuous set-valued map of Sigma at sector contacts, so plug-in classification and the ordinary bootstrap need not give uniform coverage. Generic set-inversion theory does not itself settle this OU problem because strict diffusion and nonzero-edge constraints can make the model image nonclosed, allowing an estimated covariance region to have empty intersection with the model. The new proof must show that retaining the true Sigma covers its full polarity set, define a measurable nearest-model fallback on empty intersections, and turn explicit certificate clearance into uniform root-n singleton recovery.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable random subset of {+,-} with finite-sample coverage uniformly over the compact constrained OU class, plus a theorem that it equals the true singleton uniformly whenever certificate clearance exceeds an explicit constant times n^(-1/2).

writing_exemplar.why: It explains why qualitative drift signs are the estimand under stationary-snapshot scale ambiguity; the new arc can continue from population compatibility to honest uncertainty quantification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Stationary snapshots identify at most qualitative drift information -> signature sets encode what each covariance permits -> sampling noise crosses sign frontiers -> report an honest set of cycle polarities instead of a brittle plug-in label

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a confidence region or sample criterion for the regular observable parameter and propagate it through existential model feasibility to cover the whole identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a finite identified set obtained through feasibility, so confidence-region inversion is structurally matched to the required resolution.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze directional derivatives and tangent cones of a boundary map, replacing invalid smooth-bootstrap reasoning with locally valid inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Polarity-sector contacts make the covariance-to-set map nondifferentiable in exactly the regime their theory isolates.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the population signature-set feasibility definition as the target map evaluated over every covariance retained by the confidence region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That definition supplies the qualitative causal object whose sampling uncertainty must be covered.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the sharp local minimax separation rate for recovering a singleton cycle-polarity set near every regular contact stratum of the constrained bivariate Gaussian OU model, with a matching Gaussian lower bound on compact contact subcharts.

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes population identifiable and non-identifiable regimes but gives no local statistical experiment or recovery lower bound at their interfaces.
source_refs.author: Gijs van Seeventer and Saber Salehkaleybar
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 337

source_refs.claim: Weakly regular parameters are locally degree-zero transforms of regular parameters, and consistent or equivariant estimation is impossible at identification failure.
source_refs.author: Tetsuya Kaji

source_refs.claim: For non-Gaussian continuous Lyapunov models, higher cumulants can generically identify drift and support asymptotically normal estimation; Gaussian snapshots lack that additional information.
source_refs.author: Cecilie Olesen Recke and Niels Richard Hansen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kaji's general weak-identification theory explains nonregular qualitative parameters but does not identify the reduced-form coordinates, tangent directions, or Fisher metric of this constrained OU covariance model. Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar stop at population feasibility, whereas Recke and Hansen obtain smooth drift recovery only after adding non-Gaussian higher-cumulant information. The Gaussian destination instead requires a LAN expansion for iid N(0,Sigma) on each contact subchart and a proof connecting signed normal displacement from the semialgebraic polarity frontier to testing risk. No model-specific minimax polarity bound was found.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic Gaussian experiment indexed by normal displacement from each regular contact stratum, yielding an n^(-1/2) necessary separation for uniform singleton recovery and a two-point or Gaussian-shift lower bound matching the confidence-inversion upper rate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its population trichotomy supplies the destination framing; the lower-bound problem asks how much sampling information separates its adjacent regimes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cycle polarity is identifiable at some covariances and ambiguous at others -> these regimes meet at contact surfaces -> finite samples cannot distinguish closer alternatives than the experiment's noise scale -> characterize the sharp recovery boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Represent polarity as a degree-zero transform of a minimal regular covariance displacement and derive impossibility from its local Gaussian limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At contact, covariance is regular while the singleton sign decision is a discontinuous qualitative transform.

method_exemplars.technique: Use tangent-cone and directional-differentiability analysis to identify contact-specific local geometry and its nonstandard Gaussian functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The lower bound is indexed by the same tangent geometry that governs locally valid upper inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use signature-set feasibility to specify observationally adjacent polarity hypotheses before calculating Gaussian covariance divergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact population hypotheses between which local testing is required.

literature_map:
Varando and Hansen (2020, UAI; arXiv:2005.10483) introduced graphical continuous Lyapunov models for iid equilibrium snapshots and Lyapunov-loss structure learning.
Fitch (2019; arXiv:1906.08050) independently formulated directed Gaussian interaction models and sparse Lyapunov estimation.
Dettling, Homs, Amendola, Drton, and Hansen (2023, SIMAX; arXiv:2209.03835) proved global drift identifiability exactly for simple graphs under fixed diagonal volatility; directed 2-cycles are the sharp obstruction.
That 2023 analysis concerns full parameter uniqueness, not graph-level sign quotients of a nontrivial fiber.
Dettling, Drton, and Kolar (2024, CLeaR; arXiv:2208.13572) proved Lyapunov-lasso model-selection consistency but found its irrepresentability condition surprisingly restrictive.
Hansen (2025, Algebraic Statistics; arXiv:2407.21223) developed a Lyapunov trek rule; cyclic expansions remain infinite while acyclic formulas become polynomial.
Boege et al. (2025, SPA; DOI:10.1016/j.spa.2025.104604) characterized graph-implied conditional independences of stationary diffusions and showed why covariance information differs from DAG separation.
Amendola, Boege, Hollering, and Misra (2025; arXiv:2510.04985) characterized model equivalence for acyclic GCLMs, leaving the directed 2-cycle fiber outside their scope.
Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar (2026, UAI; arXiv:2603.08311) introduced edge-sign identifiability with unknown diagonal diffusion, proved a population trichotomy, and explicitly left subgraph and graph-level signs open.
Their selected cyclic examples concern individual target edges; the scan found no exact compatibility region for the product of both edges of a bounded, trace-normalized bivariate feedback cycle.
Recke and Hansen (2026; arXiv:2603.17142) use non-Gaussian higher cumulants for generic drift recovery and asymptotic normality; Gaussian snapshots remove that information.
Lorch, Krause, and Scholkopf (2024, AISTATS; arXiv:2310.17405) learn stationary diffusions via kernel stationarity discrepancy but do not derive sharp Gaussian Lyapunov sign frontiers.
Sokol and Hansen (2014, EJP; arXiv:1304.0217) provide intervention semantics supporting a causal interpretation of OU drift entries and cycle polarity.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007), Fang and Santos (2019), and Kaji (2021) provide adjacent set-inversion, boundary, and weak-identification machinery, but no scanned paper applies it to Gaussian OU cycle-polarity contacts.
